inventory.description: Pure, host-testable products of Packages/VisualCore: VisualCoreMath, VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreScenes, VisualCoreShaderSource, VisualCoreEffectsGraph, VisualCoreDiagnostics, VisualCoreAudioDSP, VisualCorePersistence, VisualCoreParameters, VisualCoreExperience (+ VisualCoreTestSupport for test targets). iOS products of Packages/VisualCoreRendering: VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects, VisualCoreUI, VisualCoreAudio, VisualCoreAutomation, VisualCoreExperienceHost. For Light Maze (checked 2026-11-15): VisualCoreMath has Vec2 (dot, scalar cross, length, normalized, distance, isFinite; no reflect, perpendicular or rotate), Mat3 (rotation, translation, scale, trs), Camera2D and Ray3/RayHit3 (3D only: ray against box, sphere and triangle); VisualCoreSimulation has AABB2D, BroadPhase2D, Shape2D (circle and box only), Pose2D, Contacts2D, Collision2D (circle and capsule overlap, closest point on a capsule's segment, swept circles; no ray cast), Timeline, the accessibility planners (AnnouncementPlanner, HapticPlanner, StateSign) and preferences (EffectiveAccessibility with Reduce Motion and Reduce Flashing); VisualCoreScenes has Primitive (rect, circle, line with width, polygon, polyline; bounded), SceneNode (transforms, draw list, hit testing), the gesture recognizers and GestureArbiter; VisualCoreRendering has PrimitiveRenderer, RenderTarget, ResourceRegistry, PingPongTarget and TrailLayer; VisualCoreEffects has EffectRenderer and EffectScene (with the Reduce Flashing limiter); VisualCoreEffectsGraph has the pass schemas (blur, bloom, composite, flashLimit), EffectGraphValidator and FlashLimiterModel. Missing in every framework product (grep 2026-11-15): a 2D ray cast against segments, reflection about a normal, a tile board, an undo history, a progression model and any graph search or solver.

RenderHost (@MainActor) owns the EGL display, context and surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend, the CAMetalLayer RenderView, the FrameScheduler (CADisplayLink) and context generations; pause/resume, replaceScene, recreateContext, renderOffscreen and destroy; scenes implement RenderScene setup/resize/render/teardown. All EGL and GL work runs on the main thread. Light Maze's board, tracer and solver are GPU-free CPU work done on input (a move, a rotation, a level load), never in the render callback; drawing reads the tracer's segments and never decides whether a level is solved.

ResourceRegistry creates buffers, textures, programs and render targets under a ResourceBudget and rejects stale handles after a generation change. ShaderProgram, ShaderBundle and ShaderLibrary (#include expansion with line maps) compile bundled GLSL; the vc/ library holds color, field, hash, noise, palette and sdf helpers. Pipeline = ShaderProgram + RenderState, applied by GLState.apply; RenderState.additive blends additively without depth writes. PrimitiveRenderer draws a SceneNode tree (rect, circle, line with width, polygon, polyline) through a Camera2D. EffectRenderer runs a validated EffectGraphDescription (blur, bloom, composite, flashLimit among the pass schemas) into PingPong and owned render targets; EffectScene wraps any RenderScene with a graph and appends the flash limiter when Reduce Flashing is on.

Vec2, Mat3 and Camera2D (VisualCoreMath) give 2D vectors, transforms and the screen-to-world mapping; Primitive and SceneNode (VisualCoreScenes) give bounded 2D shapes in a transform tree with hit testing; TapRecognizer, DragRecognizer, RotateRecognizer and the other recognizers with GestureArbiter turn touches into deterministic gestures; Collision2D and Contacts2D (VisualCoreSimulation) cover circle, capsule and box contacts. No 2D ray cast against segments and no reflection exist (G-RAYCAST2D); snapping to a grid and to 90- or 45-degree steps is not part of any recognizer (G-SNAP).

ExperienceSession opens, checkpoints, closes and recovers an Experience on one RenderHost, applies the quality level (QualityGovernor over the experience's QualityProfile, fed by DeviceConditions thermal state and Low Power Mode) and memory/scene-phase events; ExperienceShell adapts an ExperiencePresenter (scene, controls) to Experience; ExperienceCore is the GPU-free state with its qualityTiers; ExperienceStorage is the per-experience sandbox; ExperienceFeedback routes haptics and announcements; ScenarioRunner replays a ScenarioManifest; the one app registers experiences in ExperienceRegistry and Catalog/registrations.json (twelve registered, A01-A12; Light Maze absent), and scripts/check_experience_packages.py forbids unregistered experience targets.

XcodeGen spec project.yml for the one app (target VisualCore), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, app tests via scripts/xcodebuild_app.py, and scripts/release_check.py: 118 named steps listed by --list on 2026-11-15 (shared checks including app-contracts, which checks every docs/apps/*/visualcore-contract.json, package and app builds/tests, experience-release and copy-claims steps, verify steps of A01-A12 on iOS 27 and 26, release audits of the one app, the seven reference regression steps and the ProjectM independence check).

Light Maze owns its domain (the board document with grid size, tiles and orientations; the emitter, wall, mirror, target and prism tiles and their optical rules; the bounce cap, cycle detection and epsilon policy of the tracer built on G-RAYCAST2D; the 20 handcrafted levels and their solvability proofs; level select, unlock progression, undo and restart; the beam styling with capped glow and colour plus sign cues; hints and the spoken board description; saved progress; copy and content licenses) and UI under Packages/ExperiencesCreative/LightMaze/ (Core GPU-free, CoreTests, Experience with Adapter/, ExperienceTests, Shaders, scenario-manifest.json; created in A13-P01, not present today). VisualCore owns reusable machinery: 2D vectors, transforms, the 2D camera and the 2D ray cast with reflection to come (VisualCoreMath), primitives, the scene graph and gestures (VisualCoreScenes), accessibility planners (VisualCoreSimulation), primitive drawing, render targets and effects (VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects), quality, persistence and storage (constitution Principle II, A13 section). Neon Arcade's glow layer, Oscilloscope Studio's beam polylines and Physics Playground's 2D editing stay experience code and are not copied. ProjectM stays in the harness.

Reference pinned at d93edd1, read-only; scripts/run_reference_baseline.py lists the ordered reference steps; scripts/check_reference_clean.py checks the submodule; the 7 release-check steps run in two chunks via release_check.py --only (reference-engine-xcframework, reference-build-projectm-ios-sim, reference-clean; reference-test-anglerendering-ios27, reference-test-anglerendering-ios26, projectm-reference-ios27, projectm-reference-ios26), recorded in the A13 regression baseline document (docs/apps/light-maze/regression-baseline.md) with the phase-start commit 57a587f9.

StateDigest fingerprints experience state so the same board and the same moves give the same digest; ScenarioManifest and ScenarioRunner replay recorded steps; Timeline and SceneClock drive deterministic animation; Primitive.bounded caps polygon and polyline points; ResourceBudget, EffectGraphValidator's memory quota, QualityProfile and QualityGovernor bound GPU memory, passes and quality levels. Board size, tile count, segment count, bounce cap and level count are Light Maze's own caps (G-BOARD, G-LEVELS).

matrix.capability: Render targets: owned off-screen colour targets and ping-pong pairs created through the resource registry under a budget, drawn through RenderHost on the main thread and rebuilt after context loss
matrix.source: brainstorm: render targets
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRenderingTests (DepthTargetTests, FloatTransferTests, PingPongTargetTests, TrailLayerTests, FrameChecksTests). Light Maze needs at most one glow target per frame (the effect graph allocates it); no new target kind is needed.

matrix.capability: Shaders: bundled GLSL compiled with includes and line maps, pipelines with render states including additive blending, and a primitive renderer for 2D shapes
matrix.source: brainstorm: shaders; constitution A13 visuals are code
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRenderingTests (PipelineTests, PrimitiveRendererTests, GLStateTests) and VisualCoreShaderSourceTests (RenderStateTests, ShaderLibrary tests). Tile and background shaders are Light Maze's own GLSL (procedural, no textures); a shader never decides whether a level is solved.

matrix.capability: Geometry and transformations: 2D vectors, rotation/translation/scale transforms, a 2D camera, bounded primitives with hit testing, and the reflection and segment math a light path needs
matrix.source: brainstorm: geometry and transformations
matrix.notes: Vectors, transforms, the camera, primitives with hit testing and the closest point on a segment exist and are tested (LinearAlgebraTests, Camera2DTests, SceneGraphTests, Collision2DTests). Missing: reflection of a direction about a normal, a perpendicular, and a ray-segment intersection (Vec2 has dot, scalar cross, length, normalized and distance only). These are generic: G-RAYCAST2D (VisualCoreMath, A13-P01). A13-P01 (G-RAYCAST2D closed): Ray2 casts against Segment2 lists and Vec2.reflected mirrors a direction about a normal (Ray2Tests: 360 angles × 3 normals, incidence = reflection within 1e-12).

matrix.capability: Touch controls: tap, drag and rotate recognizers with deterministic arbitration, hit testing of tiles, and gesture alternatives for single-finger use
matrix.source: brainstorm: touch controls
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreScenesTests (GestureTests, GestureArbiterTests, SceneGraphTests) and VisualCoreExperienceTests (GestureAlternativesTests). Snapping a drag to grid cells and a rotation to fixed steps is Light Maze's rule (row M07, G-SNAP). A13-P02: used by MazeGestures (TapRecognizer, DragRecognizer, RotateRecognizer, GestureArbiter).

matrix.capability: Compositing and visual feedback: a validated effect graph with blur, bloom and composite passes over the content scene, additive blending and a Reduce Flashing limiter
matrix.source: brainstorm: compositing and visual feedback
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreEffectsTests (EffectRendererTests, PassPixelTests) and VisualCoreEffectsGraphTests (ValidationTests, FlashLimiterModelTests). Fluid Art Playground and Generative Art Studio wrap their scenes in EffectScene. The beam's glow strength and its cap are Light Maze's styling (row M10, G-BEAMS).

matrix.capability: 20+ handcrafted levels on a tile board with emitter, wall, mirror, target and prism tiles (grid size, tile kinds, orientations, fixed and movable tiles)
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 1: 20+ handcrafted levels with emitter, wall, mirror, target and prism tiles
matrix.notes: Drawing tiles (primitives in a scene graph) and storing documents exist and are tested (SceneGraphTests, DocumentStoreTests). No tile board, tile model or optical rules exist in any framework product (grep 2026-11-15): G-BOARD (app-local, A13-P01) builds the board and tiles; G-LEVELS (app-local, A13-P03) the 20 levels. A13-P01: the board, tiles and the 20 levels (LightMazeCore Board, LevelCatalog) and plain beam lines from the tracer's segments (MazePresenter) exist; the remainder stays with G-LEVELS (progression, undo, saved progress). A13-P03 (G-LEVELS closed): progression over the 20 levels — level 1 open, solving a level opens the next, best move counts kept (LightMazeCore Progress, ProgressTests; SolutionReplayTests replays every level's recorded solution to solved).

matrix.capability: Drag and rotate pieces snapped to the grid: a movable tile follows the finger, lands in a free cell and turns in fixed steps, with tap-to-rotate as a single-finger alternative
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 2: drag/rotate snapped to the grid
matrix.notes: Recognizers, arbitration and the screen-to-world camera exist and are tested (GestureTests, GestureArbiterTests, Camera2DTests); snapping to cells and angle steps, occupancy and fixed-tile refusal are board rules: G-SNAP (app-local over the recognizers, A13-P02). A13-P02 (G-SNAP closed): MazeGestures over GestureArbiter — tap selects then turns, a drag from a turnable tile snaps at 0.35 cell to the nearest diagonal, a two-finger rotation turns once per 45°; every gesture sends only tile.select and tile.turn, which the native controls send too (MazeGestureTests).

matrix.capability: Deterministic ray propagation: a 2D ray from each emitter against tile segments, reflection about the hit normal, prism splitting, an epsilon and last-hit rule against self-intersection, a finite bounce cap and cycle detection
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 3: deterministic ray propagation with reflection and a finite bounce cap; spec edge cases mirror loops and self-intersection
matrix.notes: Only 3D rays against boxes, spheres and triangles (RayIntersectionTests) and 2D circle/capsule contacts (Collision2DTests) exist; no 2D ray against segments and no reflection exist in any framework product (grep 2026-11-15). The generic ray cast with reflection is G-RAYCAST2D (VisualCoreMath, A13-P01); the tile rules, prism split, bounce cap and cycle detection are G-BOARD (app-local, A13-P01). A13-P01 (G-RAYCAST2D and G-BOARD closed): BeamTracer traces the beam over Ray2 with grid-snapped reflection, ≤ 64 bounces per branch, ≤ 256 segments, ≤ 16 branches and loop detection; 20 levels proven by their recorded solutions; fixtures for lm-01, lm-10, lm-20 (BeamTracerTests, BeamFixtureTests, LevelCatalogTests).

matrix.capability: Level select, unlock progression, undo and restart, and success feedback when every target is lit
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 4: level select, unlock progression, undo/restart and success feedback
matrix.notes: Storage, versioned documents, sound effects and haptic planning exist and are tested (ExperienceStorageTests, DocumentStoreTests, SoundEffectPlayerTests, AccessibilityPlansTests). No undo history and no progression model exist in any framework product (grep 2026-11-15); a move list per level with undo and restart is small and tied to the board: G-LEVELS (app-local over ExperienceStorage, A13-P03); the success cue is G-FEEDBACK (app-local, A13-P04). A13-P03 (G-LEVELS closed): the Level menu lists locked levels disabled and solved ones with their best count, a locked choice is refused in words, Next level waits for the solve; the move list (at most 64) with Undo (move.undo, a13.no-moves) and Restart (MazeState schema 2, MovesTests, MazeProgressTests); progress.json through ProgressStore over ExperienceStorage, read never writes, a damaged, too-large or newer file is reported and left byte-identical (ProgressStoreTests); state schema 1 migrates to 2. The success cue stays with G-FEEDBACK (A13-P04). A13-P04 (G-FEEDBACK closed): the success cue plays once per transition to solved — words naming the level, the moves and the level that opened, a sine sweep made in code through VisualCoreAudio's SoundEffectPlayer, a success haptic through ExperienceFeedback (the person's switch and HapticPlanner's rate limit), and a border with a tick while solved (MazeFeedbackTests); a Hint control (hint.show, a13.already-solved) points at a tile that differs from the recorded solution (HintTests, MazeHintTests).

matrix.capability: Glow and colour cues that keep the beam path legible: a capped glow that never hides the beam or tiles, beam colours with a non-colour sign, contrast against the board, and no flashing under Reduce Flashing
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 5: glow and colour cues that keep the beam path legible; spec edge case glow hiding the beam
matrix.notes: Bloom and blur passes, additive blending, colour-plus-sign checking, contrast ratios and the flash limiter exist and are tested (PassPixelTests, RenderStateTests, AccessibilityPlansTests, AccessibilitySettingsSectionTests, FlashLimiterModelTests). Neon Arcade's glow layer is experience code and is not copied. The beam style (core line from exact segments, glow strength cap) is G-BEAMS (app-local, A13-P02); colour plus sign cues and contrast checks for beams, targets and tiles are G-FEEDBACK (app-local, A13-P04). A13-P02: capped static glow (halo 0.30 cell at 0.25 opacity under a 0.08 core), lit-target rings and a selection outline beside colour; the remaining hints and success feedback stay with G-FEEDBACK. A13-P04 (G-FEEDBACK closed): nine board states carry distinct non-colour signs (stateSignProblems empty) and every state colour reaches at least 3 : 1 against the board by AccessibleColors.contrastRatio, the unlit target raised from 2.1 : 1 to 3.85 : 1; the glow cap of 0.15 cell is kept (MazeStyleTests).

matrix.capability: Built-in solvability test: a bounded search over the movable tiles' cells and orientations that proves each shipping level solvable and records one solution
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 6: built-in solvability test
matrix.notes: State digests and scenario manifests exist for fixtures and replay (StateDigestTests, ScenarioManifestTests); no graph search or solver exists in any framework product (grep 2026-11-15). The search is specific to the board's rules and stays app-local: G-SOLVER (app-local, A13-P05) runs over G-BOARD's tracer.

matrix.capability: Beam geometry from the CPU tracer only: the drawn beam is exactly the tracer's segment list (polyline primitives), never recomputed in a shader or the render callback
matrix.source: cross-cutting: beam geometry single source of truth; manual main risk visual beams diverging from logical paths
matrix.notes: Polyline and line primitives drawn by PrimitiveRenderer exist and are tested (SceneGraphTests, PrimitiveRendererTests); Oscilloscope Studio draws its traces as polylines from CPU points this way (experience code). The segments come from G-RAYCAST2D and G-BOARD (A13-P01); drawing them with the glow is G-BEAMS (A13-P02), tested by comparing drawn vertices with the tracer's segments. A13-P01: the board, tiles and the 20 levels (LightMazeCore Board, LevelCatalog) and plain beam lines from the tracer's segments (MazePresenter) exist; the remainder stays with G-BEAMS (glow). A13-P02 (G-BEAMS closed): every beam core line and its halo are drawn from the tracer's exact segments (MazeGlowTests: each core equals a segment; halo half-width ≤ 0.15 cell).

matrix.capability: Determinism and replay: the same board and the same moves give the same beam paths and state digest; recorded move scenarios replay identically
matrix.source: cross-cutting: determinism and replay; constitution A13 deterministic, GPU-free rules
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreExperienceTests (StateDigestTests, ScenarioManifestTests) and VisualCoreExperienceHostTests (ScenarioRunnerTests), VisualCoreSimulationTests (TimelineTests). The tracer itself must be deterministic (fixed iteration order, no randomness): asserted by G-BOARD's tests.

matrix.capability: Bounded content: caps on primitive points, GPU memory, effect passes and quality levels, with board size, tiles, segments, bounces and levels capped by the experience
matrix.source: cross-cutting: bounded content; constitution A13 bounded; spec edge case unbounded content
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreScenesTests (SceneGraphTests), VisualCoreDiagnosticsTests (ResourceLedger and QualityProfileTests) and VisualCoreEffectsGraphTests (ValidationTests). Light Maze's own caps (grid size, tile count, segment count, bounce cap) are part of G-BOARD; the level count is part of G-LEVELS.

matrix.capability: Persistence of progress: versioned documents with migrations in the experience's own storage, refused writes leave the previous state intact
matrix.source: cross-cutting: persistence; constitution A13 offline-first and private
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCorePersistenceTests (DocumentStoreTests, migration tests) and VisualCoreExperienceTests (ExperienceStorageTests, ExperienceSnapshotTests). The progress document (unlocked and solved levels, best move counts) is G-LEVELS.

matrix.capability: Quality tiers and low power: quality governor fed by thermal state and Low Power Mode, declared tiers (glow on or off, glow radius)
matrix.source: cross-cutting: quality tiers and low power; constitution A13 bounded
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreDiagnosticsTests (QualityGovernorTests, QualityProfileTests) and VisualCoreExperienceTests (QualityDeclarationTests). Core.qualityTiers must match the presenter's levels (lesson of earlier gates); the beam's core line is drawn at every tier.

matrix.capability: Accessibility: Reduce Motion and Reduce Flashing honoured, VoiceOver announcements, a spoken board description (tiles, beam path, lit and unlit targets), colour never the only cue
matrix.source: cross-cutting: accessibility with Reduce Motion, Reduce Flashing and spoken board description; constitution A13 accessibility
matrix.notes: Preferences, announcement planning and sinks, reduced-motion durations, colour-plus-sign checks and the flash limiter exist and are tested (AccessibilityPreferencesTests, AccessibilityPlansTests, AccessibilityPlayersTests, FlashLimiterModelTests). The spoken board description and hints are specific to the board: G-FEEDBACK (app-local, A13-P04). System accessibility audits wait for device testing. A13-P04 (G-FEEDBACK closed): Describe speaks the full board (tiles by kind with rows and columns, each beam branch's start, turns and end, every target lit or unlit; at most 4,000 characters, BoardDescriptionTests); the canvas description counts lit targets; words are kept and shown with VoiceOver off and posted only while it runs; Reduce Motion and Reduce Flashing keep the solved border static (MazeFeedbackTests). System accessibility audits wait for device testing.

matrix.capability: Lifecycle and context loss: context loss, resize, background and memory warning rebuild every GPU resource; the board and progress are CPU state and survive
matrix.source: cross-cutting: lifecycle and context loss; constitution A13 resilient GPU state
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRenderingTests (RenderHostTests, context recreation) and VisualCoreExperienceHostTests (session lifecycle). Light Maze keeps no state on the GPU; the beam is redrawn from the tracer's segments after recreation.

matrix.capability: Sound and haptic feedback: procedural sound effects (no recordings), haptic planning with rate limits, routed through the experience feedback channel
matrix.source: cross-cutting: sound and haptic feedback
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreAudioDSPTests (SoundEffectSynthTests), VisualCoreAudioTests (SoundEffectPlayerTests), VisualCoreSimulationTests (AccessibilityPlansTests) and VisualCoreUITests (AccessibilityPlayersTests). Which cue plays on a snap, a lit target and a solved level is G-FEEDBACK.

matrix.capability: Licenses and provenance: every level, palette and shader bundled later records its author and license; only original content; third-party notices in the acknowledgements
matrix.source: cross-cutting: licenses; constitution A13 licenses; spec FR-A13-006
matrix.notes: LicenseInventory and AcknowledgementsView cover third-party notices (AcknowledgementsViewTests; scripts/check_licenses.py audits the built app); per-content author and license fields for levels, palettes and shaders do not exist in a framework product and belong to the experience's content data, as Physics Playground's LicenseAudit does: part of G-LEVELS (app-local, A13-P03), checked again at release QA with G-SOLVER (A13-P05). A13-P03 (G-LEVELS closed): every one of the 20 levels records its author and license and LicenseAudit checks them against the committed content-licenses document (LicenseAuditTests); release QA rechecks with G-SOLVER (A13-P05).

gaps.justification: Found in A13-P00: Vec2 has no reflect or perpendicular, Ray3/RayHit3 are 3D only and no 2D ray against segments exists in any framework product; Collision2D gives only the closest point on a capsule's segment. A 2D ray cast against line segments (nearest hit distance, point, segment index and normal, with a minimum distance so a ray leaving a surface does not hit it again) and reflection of a direction about a normal are generic geometry and belong to VisualCoreMath (constitution A13 reuse first, clarification 5, A13-P01); tile semantics stay in the experience.
gaps.test: Host tests (swift test, no GPU): rays hit segments at the analytic distance, point and normal, including endpoints, grazing and parallel cases; misses return nil; the nearest of several segments wins and ties break by a stable order; the minimum distance skips the segment just left; reflection about axis-aligned and 45-degree normals matches the analytic result and preserves length; NaN/Inf inputs rejected; API baseline additive, documented with ///, and the reference regression passes at the X gate

gaps.justification: No tile board, tile model or optical rules exist in any framework product. The grid, the emitter, wall, mirror, target and prism tiles with orientations, the optical rules (mirror reflection via G-RAYCAST2D, prism split, wall absorption, target lighting), the epsilon and last-hit policy, the bounce cap, cycle detection and the board caps are Light Maze's puzzle rules and stay in its GPU-free Core (clarification 5, A13-P01).
gaps.test: Core host tests: fixture boards give the expected segment lists and lit targets; mirror loops stop by cycle detection and long paths stop at the bounce cap with a typed reason; a ray leaving a mirror never re-hits it; the same board gives bitwise identical segments and digest on repeated runs; boards above the grid or tile caps are refused

gaps.justification: PrimitiveRenderer draws polylines and EffectRenderer runs bloom and blur, but the beam's style (core line from the tracer's exact segments, glow strength and radius capped so the beam and tiles stay legible, tier-dependent glow) is Light Maze's presentation; app-local over PrimitiveRenderer and the effect graph (clarification 5, A13-P02).
gaps.test: Experience tests: drawn beam vertices equal the tracer's segments for fixture boards; with glow off (low tier or Reduce Flashing) the core line still draws; the glow parameters stay within the declared cap; context recreation redraws the same image within a pixel tolerance

gaps.justification: The recognizers and arbiter report drags and rotations but know nothing of cells, occupancy or fixed tiles. Snapping a dragged tile to the nearest free cell, turning in fixed angle steps, refusing fixed tiles and offering tap-to-rotate are board rules, app-local over the gesture recognizers (clarification 5, A13-P02).
gaps.test: Core and experience tests: drags end in the nearest free cell or return to the start; rotations land on the allowed steps; fixed tiles refuse moves; tap-to-rotate gives the same board as the rotate gesture; every move changes the board only through the core and retraces the beam

gaps.justification: No progression model or undo history exists in any framework product. The 20 handcrafted levels with author and license records, level select, unlock progression, the per-level move list with undo and restart, and the versioned progress document are Light Maze's content and state, app-local over ExperienceStorage, DocumentStore and MigrationChain (clarification 5, A13-P03).
gaps.test: Core host tests: 20 levels load and validate against the board caps; each records author and license; solving a level unlocks the next; undo restores the previous board exactly and restart restores the level's start; progress round-trips through storage with migration, and a refused write keeps the previous progress

gaps.justification: Announcement and haptic planners, sinks, colour-plus-sign checks and sound effects exist; hints, the spoken board description (tiles, beam path, lit and unlit targets), colour plus sign cues for beams, targets and tiles with contrast checks, and the success cue with sound and haptics are specific to the board, app-local over the accessibility planners and sound effects (clarification 5, A13-P04).
gaps.test: Core and experience tests: the board description names every tile, the beam path and each target's state for fixture boards; every beam and target state has a distinct non-colour sign (stateSignProblems empty) and meets the contrast threshold; the success cue plays once per solve and respects the haptic rate limit; Reduce Motion shortens transitions and Reduce Flashing removes pulsing

gaps.justification: No graph search or solver exists in any framework product. A bounded search over the movable tiles' cells and orientations, using G-BOARD's tracer, that proves each shipping level solvable and records one solution is specific to Light Maze's rules and stays app-local (clarification 5, A13-P05).
gaps.test: Core host tests: every shipping level is proven solvable within the search's node cap and its recorded solution lights every target when replayed; an unsolvable fixture is reported unsolvable; the search is deterministic and refuses boards above the cap

negative.source: ADR-0009; constitution A13 reuse first; CLAUDE.md rule 1; spec edge cases

reasons: A working host and 2D drawing path exist: RenderHost on OpenGL ES -> ANGLE -> Metal, PrimitiveRenderer drawing rect, circle, line, polygon and polyline primitives of a SceneNode tree through Camera2D, and EffectRenderer/EffectScene running blur, bloom and composite passes with the Reduce Flashing limiter, all public and tested.
